story.description: Create a reusable header block for the Disney Imagination Campus homepage. The block must present the observed contact prompt and phone number, the Contact Us entry, the Disney Imagination Campus logo/link where available from rendered evidence, a search control where available from rendered evidence, and the primary navigation labels ABOUT US, CURRICULUM & TICKETS, SPECIAL EVENTS, PLAN YOUR TRIP, and CONNECT WITH US. The header is a shared component pattern observed on the homepage and the connect-with-us page, with a header landmark present in the captured homepage data. Exact typography, spacing, colors, hover behavior, and destination URLs were not captured and must remain configurable.
accessibilityCriteria: The header is exposed as a page header landmark and all interactive header items are reachable by keyboard in a logical order.
All interactive controls and links have accessible names matching or clearly representing their visible labels, including Contact Us and the primary navigation labels.

implementationAnalysis.rationale: The story requires a reusable header block that renders the captured contact content (Questions?, Call (321) 939 7560, Contact Us) and primary navigation labels (ABOUT US, CURRICULUM & TICKETS, SPECIAL EVENTS, PLAN YOUR TRIP, CONNECT WITH US) with configurable link destinations. The repository already contains blocks/header/header.js and blocks/header/header.css at the expected paths. The existing header.js follows the canonical EDS pattern: it loads a /nav fragment document, reads three sections (brand, sections, tools) from that fragment, and decorates them into a nav element with hamburger, brand, nav-sections, and nav-tools areas. The existing header.css provides the full nav layout including hamburger, brand, sections, and tools grid areas with responsive behaviour. The Content Agent document does NOT include a header block table — the header is a global shared component loaded via fragment convention (/nav document), not an inline page block. This is confirmed by: (1) scripts.js calls loadHeader(doc.querySelector('body > header')) in loadLazy, (2) header.js uses loadFragment(navPath) where navPath defaults to '/nav', (3) the repository inventory shows fragmentSupport.conventions.navigation = '/nav'. Therefore the header is NOT a content-gap block requiring a new table structure — it is a GLOBAL fragment-driven pattern. The implementation work is: modify blocks/header/header.js to support a contact bar row (row index 0 of the /nav fragment) containing the Questions? prompt, phone number, and Contact Us link, in addition to the existing brand/sections/tools rows; modify blocks/header/header.css to style the contact bar and nav-sections bar to match the captured evidence (contact bar above brand/nav, nav-sections bar with black background at y:131, height:50px, flex justify-content:center); and update styles/styles.css --nav-height to reflect the observed two-row header height (~160px desktop). The captured evidence shows: header-wrapper rect height 160px, nav element height 181px, nav-sections div at y:131 height:50px with background-color rgb(0,0,0) and justify-content:center, nav ul (menubar) max-width:1080px with justify-content:space-between. The contact bar content (Questions?, Call (321) 939 7560, Contact Us) is observed in the header region text. The logo/brand and search control are referenced in acceptance criteria as 'where available from rendered evidence' — the brand area is already handled by the existing nav-brand section; a search control is not present in the captured computed-style evidence for the header region and must be flagged as a content gap. The /nav fragment document must be authored by the Content Agent with four sections: (0) contact bar, (1) brand/logo, (2) nav sections list, (3) tools/search — but since the Content Agent document does not include this fragment, it is flagged as a content gap. The JS and CSS changes are scoped entirely to blocks/header/ and a --nav-height token update in styles/styles.css.

The primary navigation renders the captured labels exactly as observed: ABOUT US, CURRICULUM & TICKETS, SPECIAL EVENTS, PLAN YOUR TRIP, and CONNECT WITH US.

assumptions: The /nav fragment document is the authoritative source for all header content. It must be authored by the Content Agent with four sections: (0) contact bar paragraph(s), (1) brand/logo, (2) nav UL, (3) tools. This fragment is NOT present in the Content Agent document and is flagged as a CONTENT GAP — the workflow must report this to the Content Agent before the header can be fully validated.

The search control referenced in AC4 is not confirmed in the captured computed-style evidence for the header region. The nav-tools area (section[3] of the fragment) will accommodate it if authored, but no search-specific JS or CSS will be added speculatively.

The observed nav-sections transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,-720,0) is a capture artefact from a translated/scrolled element during the Playwright capture and does not represent a real CSS transform to replicate.

The --nav-height token update to ~160px applies to the desktop breakpoint. The existing mobile grid layout in header.css uses the same token for the hamburger/brand row height; the contact bar will add to the total header height on mobile via natural flow, so the token update is scoped to the desktop media query (width >= 900px) to avoid breaking the mobile hamburger layout.

The existing header.js fragment-loading convention (/nav path from metadata or default) is preserved unchanged. The four-section structure is a superset of the existing three-section structure — section[0] is new (contact bar), sections[1-3] map to existing brand/sections/tools.

The black background of the nav-sections bar (rgb(0,0,0)) is grounded in the captured computed style evidence and is expressed as a CSS custom property --nav-sections-bg set in styles.css, consumed by header.css, making it overridable without touching block files.
No new block folder is created. The implementation is entirely within the existing blocks/header/ directory and the styles/styles.css token file.

risks.risk: CONTENT GAP: /nav fragment document not present in Content Agent output
risks.mitigation: Flag to Content Agent. The header block JS and CSS can be implemented and committed, but end-to-end rendering requires the /nav fragment to be authored with the four-section structure. The workflow should block final validation until the fragment is available.

risks.risk: Four-section fragment structure breaks existing three-section assumption in header.js
risks.mitigation: The modified header.js will use defensive index checks (if (nav.children[i])) already present in the existing code. Section[0] (contact) is new; sections[1-3] map to existing brand/sections/tools. If the fragment only has three sections (no contact bar), the block degrades gracefully to the existing behaviour.

risks.risk: --nav-height token change may affect other blocks or page layout that depend on the 64px value
risks.mitigation: Scope the token update to the desktop media query only. Audit styles.css and header.css usages: only header { height: var(--nav-height) } and the nav grid-template row height use this token. The main element starts at y:160 in the captured evidence, confirming the 160px value is correct for desktop.

risks.risk: Search control not captured — if the live site has a search input in the header tools area, the nav-tools section will render it from the fragment but without specific styling
risks.mitigation: nav-tools CSS already exists in header.css. Search-specific styling can be added in a follow-on story once the search control is confirmed and captured.

risks.risk: Logo image asset not captured — brand image src is unknown
risks.mitigation: The brand image will be authored into the /nav fragment by the Content Agent. The existing nav-brand CSS (width:128px) will apply. No hardcoded image URL is added.
